speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. To better understand your condition, have you noticed any rash or skin lesions anywhere on your body besides your wrists?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection (DGI).

The combination of a migratory joint pain pattern (knee then wrist), fever, chills, and the specific history of sexual activity with a recent camping trip (which may be a distractor or co-incidental) strongly suggests an ascending gonococcal infection. The skin lesions you mentioned in your initial prompt, combined with the tenosynovitis-like presentation at the wrist, are classic for DGI. I am requesting blood cultures and a Gram stain of the synovial fluid to confirm.
